blocks.text: B2-23 · INT-A and INT-B exercises
Lesson overview

This drive closes the INT track of B2 with two complete exercises, which bring together what you have learned in the four modules. INT-A is the written analysis of an article in Arabic from open sources: reading without vowels, understanding, attribution and degree of certainty, facts and opinions, signals of disinformation, translation of key steps and an analysis relationship in English with a synthesis in Arabic. INT-B is an information interview in Arabic, like that of a journalist (B2-07): preparation, questions, conduction with questions for further analysis and reformulations, verification of data and faithful report. Both have a heading; To overcome them, at least 3 on 4 in every criterion. The method is that of journalism and analysis of open sources: public texts, people who speak voluntarily in public, no operational techniques. Four weeks, while MAG closes...03.

rows: B2 · Module B2.4 Variation and production INT trace

blocks.text: Materials This unit, authentic items of Arabic newspapers and institutional pages (Appendix C), a recorder, sessions with tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. analyze an Arabic article without vowels 400–500 words in 90 minutes, with a six-step method;
2. write an analysis report in English (300 words) with summary, sources, degree of certainty, opinions, gaps and
translated quotations;
3. write a neutral synthesis in Arabic (100 words);
4. prepare and conduct an informational interview with 15 minutes in fuṣḥā Talked, with open questions, about
precision and deepening;
5. write a faithful account of the interview, distinguishing what has been said, what has not been said and
what needs to be verified. Four-week plan.

2. INT-A task and address book

The task. An authentic or realistic Arabic article (400–500 words, without vowels). In 90 minutes, with the dictionary only: 1) timed reading (lens ≥ 90 words per minute); 2) analysis report in English (about 300 words, section 4); 3) translation of two key paragraphs chosen by the examiner; 4) Neutral synthesis in Arabic (approximately 100 words).

blocks.text: The source map is at the heart of the analysis. An example:
4. The analysis report
The report is written in English, in short paragraphs with titles, in neutral tone. Recommended structure:
1. References: tested, date, author, gender.
2. Summary (3–4 lines): the main fact, who, what, when.
3. Sources and locations: for each, what it says and with what degree of certainty (from the map).
4. Opinions and connotations: where the text evaluates, with the words quoted in Arabic and translated.
5. Lacks and signals: what is missing; any misinformation signals (INT-05).
6. Language notes: ambiguous words, translation choices, variety (if there are quotes in dialect, B2-21).

Useful formulas in English. According to the Ministry... • • • The Party supports, without providing evidence, that... • • • Anonymous sources quoted in the newspaper consider it likely that... · • • The article does not indicate the position of... · • • The adjective X (in Arabic ...) introduces a positive assessment. · • • It is not clear if...; the text admits two readings: ... ... ....
5. Pronunciation

The final timed reading. Layer B2 asks for a silent reading of at least 90 words per minute, with a correct synthesis. Twice a week, read a new article by 350–400 words with the stopwatch and record the time and quality of the oral synthesis of one minute. If you stay under 90 words per minute, do not reread the phrases already understood: mark with the pencil and go ahead; You're only going back to the words marked after the first reading.

You have 20 minutes to prepare yourself on a presentation card, 15 minutes of interview in fuṣḥā spoken (recorded), 30 minutes for the English report (200 words) with three translated Arabic quotes.

blocks.text: The golden rule. The report does not add what the interviewee did not say and does not diminish his statements:         • said that the beneficiaries are "about two thousand" • does not become "the beneficiaries" are two thousand.
10. New lexicon

Notes of use. ⁧المَصَادِرُ المَفْتُوحَةُ⁩ indicates publicly accessible information (printing, institutional sites, publications, transmissions). ⁧مَجْهُول⁩ is also used for the passive ( ⁧المَبْنِيُّ لِلْمَجْهُولِ⁩ , B2-16): Built for the unknown. ⁧مَحْضَر⁩ is the minutes of a meeting ( ⁧مَحْضَرُ الاِجْتِمَاعِ⁩ ) and, in the judicial field, an act: in this course we use it for the account of an interview.
